summary.text: King of Argos, son of Triopas in Pausanias' native succession and father of Io; Apollodorus instead makes him son of Argus and Ismene, while Castor and the tragedians name Inachus as Io's father.
Not Iasus the Athenian captain slain by Aeneas at the ships, nor Iasus of Arcadia who exposed Atalanta, nor other homonymous Iasus figures in the genealogies.

story.text: Apollodorus says Argus and Ismene, daughter of Asopus, had a son Iasus who is said to have been the father of Io — but the annalist Castor and many of the tragedians allege that Io was a daughter of Inachus, and Hesiod and Acusilaus say she was a daughter of Piren.

Pausanias' Argive king-list makes Iasus son of Triopas and father of Io, who went to Egypt — whether the circumstances be as Herodotus records or as the Greeks say. After Iasus, Crotopus son of Agenor succeeded before Danaus returned from Egypt.
The lineage note preserved at Argos adds that Iasus was father of Io, whom Hera's jealousy drove from the land — and of the twin kings who would divide the kingdom after the age of Danaus.
